Class LtsvFormatterBuilder

java.lang.Object
io.jstach.rainbowgum.format.LtsvFormatterBuilder
All Implemented Interfaces:
LogBuilder<LtsvFormatterBuilder, LogFormatter>
public final class LtsvFormatterBuilder extends Object implements LogBuilder<LtsvFormatterBuilder, LogFormatter>
Builder to create LogFormatter. Formats events as LTSV (Labeled Tab-separated Values), one line of tab separated label:value fields per event, selected with the ltsv encoder scheme.

Each event is written as one line, for example (⇥ is a tab): time:2026-10-05T15:04:05.123Z⇥level:INFO⇥logger:com.example.App⇥threadId:1⇥threadName:main⇥msg:hello world⇥requestId:42

  • The labels are logfmt's field names. The thread fields are chosen with ThreadFields, by default threadId and threadName.
  • The fields listed as columns (see EventField) come first, in the order listed and without labels, so they are read by position. With columns=time,level,logger,thread,msg: 2026-10-05T15:04:05.123Z⇥INFO⇥com.example.App⇥1⇥main⇥hello world⇥requestId:42. The fields not listed follow with their labels, before the key values. With columns=thread,msg: 1⇥main⇥hello world⇥time:2026-10-05T15:04:05.123Z⇥level:INFO⇥logger:com.example.App⇥requestId:42. Output with columns is no longer LTSV.
  • time is the UTC instant with milliseconds by default, and timestamp chooses another format or a DateTimeFormatter pattern in UTC, as for TTLL.
  • level is TRACE, DEBUG, INFO, WARN, or ERROR, unpadded by default.
  • A field set to none is not written, and cannot be a column.
  • The key values follow the fields, in order. A key value named like one of these fields is prefixed with keyValues.. A key value without a value is written with an empty one.
  • A throwable adds error (its toString()) and stacktrace.
Values are never quoted. LTSV does not allow tab, newline, or carriage return in a value, so these and \ are backslash escaped (\t, \n, \r, \\) and other control characters are written as \uXXXX, so every event stays on one line. Characters LTSV does not allow in labels (anything but A-Z a-z 0-9 _ . -) are percent-encoded as UTF-8 (a b is a%20b), and an empty key is %, so different keys stay different.

Values can be colored like the TTLL formatter; labels and msg are not. error and stacktrace take the level's color, since they are on the event's line.
